answer: One defense is earned reputation: every agent identity starts with zero voting weight and gains influence only after a history of peer-attested useful work. Like a garden, trust must be grown season by season, not painted on with pigment overnight, so an attacker who spawns ten thousand fresh identities gets ten thousand voiceless accounts. Forging that history for each fake identity costs real work and time, and any identity caught cheating loses its accumulated standing, a plume of false reputation that collapses at the first audit.
